## Task 1

## Data Acquisition

### State Electricity Profiles (EIA)

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
library(httr2)
library(rvest)

get_eia_sep <- function(state, abbr){
    library(tidyverse)
    library(stringr)
    library(httr2)
    library(rvest)
    library(fs)
  
    state_formatted <- str_to_lower(state) |> str_replace_all("\\s", "")
    
    dir_name <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
    file_name <- fs::path(dir_name, state_formatted)
    
    fs::dir_create(dir_name, recurse=TRUE)
    
    if(!fs::file_exists(file_name)){
        BASE_URL <- "https://www.eia.gov"
        RESPONSE <- request(BASE_URL) |> 
          req_url_path("electricity", 
                       "state", 
                       state_formatted) |>
          req_headers(
            `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
            ) |>   
          req_retry(
                max_tries = 4, 
          ) |>
          req_perform(file_name)
    
        resp_check_status(RESPONSE)
    }
    
    TABLE <- read_html(file_name) |> 
        html_element("table") |> 
        html_table() |>
        mutate(Item = str_to_lower(Item))
    
    if("U.S. rank" %in% colnames(TABLE)){
        TABLE <- TABLE |> rename(Rank = `U.S. rank`)
    }
    
    CO2_MWh <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "carbon dioxide (lbs/mwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |> 
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    PRIMARY <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "primary energy source") |> 
        pull(Rank)
    
    RATE <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "average retail price (cents/kwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        as.numeric()
    
    GENERATION_MWh <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "net generation (megawatthours)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    data.frame(CO2_MWh               = CO2_MWh, 
               primary_source        = PRIMARY,
               electricity_price_MWh = RATE * 10, # / 100 cents to dollars &
               # * 1000 kWh to MWH 
               generation_MWh        = GENERATION_MWh, 
               state                 = state, 
               abbreviation          = abbr
    )
}

EIA_SEP_REPORT <- map2(state.name, state.abb, get_eia_sep) |> list_rbind()
```

### Energy Consumption (NTD)

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
load_ntd_energy <- function(){
  library(readxl)
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_ENERGY_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_energy.xlsx")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://www.transit.dot.gov/") |>
      req_url_path("sites",
                   "fta.dot.gov",
                   "files",
                   "2026-09",
                   "2025 Energy Consumption_260806.xlsx") |> 
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Energy File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_energy.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  to_numeric_fill_0 <- function(x){
    x <- if_else(x == "-", NA, x)
    replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  }

  read_excel(NTD_ENERGY_FILE) |> 
    select(-c(`Reporter Type`, 
              `Reporting Module`, 
              `Gallons of Other Fuel`, 
              `Other Fuel Description`)) |>
    mutate(across(-c(`Agency Name`, 
                     `Mode`,
                     `TOS`), 
                  to_numeric_fill_0)) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Mode`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum), 
              .groups = "keep") |>
    mutate(ENERGY = sum(c_across(c(where(is.numeric))))) |>
    filter(ENERGY > 0) |>
    select(-ENERGY) |>
    ungroup()
}

NTD_ENERGY <- load_ntd_energy()
```

### Transit Service Provided (NTD)

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
load_ntd_service <- function(){
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv") |>
      req_url_query(`$query`=paste(
        "SELECT  `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`", 
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000", 
        sep=",")) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Service File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_service.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  read_csv(NTD_SERVICE_FILE) |>
    mutate(flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate))
}

NTD_SERVICE <- load_ntd_service()
```

## Task 3a: State Electricity Profiles

```{r}
library(gt)

# Q2: the 5 states with the highest CO2 per MWh
dirtiest_states <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  arrange(desc(CO2_MWh)) |>               
  head(5) |>                              
  select(state, primary_source, CO2_MWh)

# Q3: average CO2 per MWh, weighted by how much electricity each state makes
total_co2 <- sum(EIA_SEP_REPORT$CO2_MWh * EIA_SEP_REPORT$generation_MWh)
total_generation <- sum(EIA_SEP_REPORT$generation_MWh)
us_avg_co2_mwh <- total_co2 / total_generation

# Q5: how many times cleaner is New York than Texas?
texas <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |> filter(abbreviation == "TX")
new_york <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |> filter(abbreviation == "NY")
tx_vs_ny <- texas$CO2_MWh / new_york$CO2_MWh
```

These 5 states are the "dirtiest" West Virginia, Kentucky, Wyoming, Missouri, and Hawaii. Which means they produce the most CO2 per megawatt-hour.

```{r}
dirtiest_states |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(state = "State", primary_source = "Primary Source",
             CO2_MWh = "CO2 (lbs per MWh)") |>
  fmt_number(CO2_MWh, decimals = 0) |>
  tab_source_note("Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration state profiles")
```

On average `r round(us_avg_co2_mwh)` pounds of CO2 is emitted per megawatt-hour.

New York is about `r round(tx_vs_ny, 1)` cleaner than Texas in terms of CO2 emission per MWh.

## Task 3b: NTD Energy Usage

```{r}
# Q1: the 5 agencies that used the most gallons of fuel, broken down by type
# (electricity is in kWh and hydrogen is in kg, so they are not part of "gallons")
top_fuel_agencies <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  group_by(`Agency Name`) |>
  summarize(
    diesel    = sum(`Gallons of Diesel Fuel`),
    gasoline  = sum(`Gallons of Gasoline`),
    cng       = sum(`Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas`),
    lpg       = sum(`Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas`),
    biodiesel = sum(`Gallons of Bio-Diesel`),
    other     = sum(`Gallons of Bunker Fuel`) + sum(`Gallons of Ethanol`) +
                sum(`Gallons of Kerosene`) + sum(`Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas`)
  ) |>
  mutate(total = diesel + gasoline + cng + lpg + biodiesel + other) |>
  arrange(desc(total)) |>
  head(5)
```

NJ Transit Corporation, NYC MTA, LA County MTA, Northeast Illinois Regional Commuter Railroad, and Massachusetts Bay Transport are the top 5 leading agencies in fuel. 4 of which mainly use diesel, with the exception LA which leads in compressed natural gas.

```{r}
top_fuel_agencies |>
  select(`Agency Name`, total, diesel, gasoline, cng, lpg, biodiesel, other) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(`Agency Name` = "Agency", total = "Total Gallons",
             diesel = "Diesel", gasoline = "Gasoline", cng = "CNG",
             lpg = "LPG", biodiesel = "Bio-Diesel", other = "Other") |>
  fmt_number(c(total, diesel, gasoline, cng, lpg, biodiesel, other),
             decimals = 0) |>
  tab_source_note("Source: National Transit Database, 2025 energy consumption")
```

## Task 3c: NTD Service

```{r}
# Q1 (graph): the 5 transit services with the most unlinked passenger trips (UPT)
# A "service" here is one agency running one mode (for example, buses)
top_upt <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  group_by(AGENCY, mode) |>
  summarize(upt = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(service = paste0(AGENCY, " (", mode, ")")) |>
  arrange(desc(upt)) |>
  head(5)

ggplot(top_upt, aes(x = reorder(service, upt), y = upt)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = scales::label_wrap(30)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title = "Top 5 US Transit Services by Annual Trips",
       x = NULL, y = "Unlinked passenger trips, 2025",
       caption = "Source: National Transit Database")
```

The graph shows which transit system across the US serves the most trips per year. With the top 2 being comprised of NYC, and the MTA heavy rail having more anuall trips than the rest of the country along with NYC buses.

```{r}
# Q2 (inline): average trip length on MTA New York City Transit
# average trip length = total passenger miles / total number of trips
mta <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  filter(AGENCY == "MTA New York City Transit")

mta_miles <- sum(mta$sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE)

```

The average length of a trip on the NYC MTA is `r round(mta_avg_trip_miles)` miles.

## Task 5: Calculate Emissions

```{r}
service_by_mode <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  group_by(NTD_ID, mode) |>
  summarize(
    state = first(state),                              # the agency's state
    total_upt = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),          # trips
    passenger_miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(NTD_ID = as.numeric(NTD_ID))   # text -> number, to match the energy table

emissions_data <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  left_join(service_by_mode,
            join_by(`NTD ID` == NTD_ID, Mode == mode)) |>
  left_join(select(EIA_SEP_REPORT, abbreviation, CO2_MWh),
            join_by(state == abbreviation)) |>
  mutate(
    used_us_avg = is.na(CO2_MWh),                      
    CO2_MWh = coalesce(CO2_MWh, us_avg_co2_mwh)      
  )

co2_diesel   <- 22.46
co2_gasoline <- 19.36
co2_kerosene <- 21.78
co2_lpg      <- 12.68
co2_bunker   <- 24.78
co2_cng      <- 117 * 0.114    
co2_lng      <- 117 * 0.0747   

emissions_data <- emissions_data |>
  mutate(

    electricity_mwh = (`Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery` +
                       `Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion`) / 1000,
    total_co2_lbs =
      `Gallons of Diesel Fuel` * co2_diesel +
      `Gallons of Bio-Diesel` * co2_diesel +
      `Gallons of Gasoline` * co2_gasoline +
      `Gallons of Kerosene` * co2_kerosene +
      `Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas` * co2_lpg +
      `Gallons of Bunker Fuel` * co2_bunker +
      `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas` * co2_cng +
      `Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas` * co2_lng +
      electricity_mwh * CO2_MWh,
    total_co2_tons = total_co2_lbs / 2204.62     # pounds -> metric tons
  )
```

I treated bio-diesel the same as regular diesel by applying the same emission factor of 22.46 pounds of CO2 per gallon. I did this because the calculation did not use a separate emission factor for bio-diesel. This means bio-diesel emissions are included in the total rather than being excluded or treated as carbon-neutral.

## Task 6: Normalize Emissions to Transit Usage

```{r}
agency_summary <- emissions_data |>
  group_by(`NTD ID`, `Agency Name`) |>
  summarize(
    state = first(state),
    total_co2_lbs = sum(total_co2_lbs),
    upt = sum(total_upt),
    passenger_miles = sum(passenger_miles),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(upt > 0, passenger_miles > 0) |>     
  mutate(
    lbs_per_trip = total_co2_lbs / upt,
    lbs_per_mile = total_co2_lbs / passenger_miles
  )

min_trips <- 100000
medium_cutoff <- 3000000
large_cutoff <- 30000000

agency_summary <- agency_summary |>
  filter(upt >= min_trips) |>
  mutate(size = case_when(
    upt >= large_cutoff ~ "Large",
    upt >= medium_cutoff ~ "Medium",
    .default = "Small"
  ))
```

Based on emissions per passenger mile, the most efficient agencies were:
- Large: Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation District of Oregon, with 0.0983 lbs of CO2 per passenger mile.
- Medium: Snohomish County Public Transportation Benefit Area Corporation, with 0.147 lbs of CO2 per passenger mile.
- Small: City of Seattle, with 0.0639 lbs of CO2 per passenger mile.

## Task 7: Award Winners

### Award 1: Greenest Transit Agency

```{r}
greenest <- agency_summary |>
  group_by(size) |>
  slice_min(lbs_per_trip, n = 1) |>
  ungroup()

size_medians <- agency_summary |>
  group_by(size) |>
  summarize(median_lbs_per_trip = median(lbs_per_trip),
            n_agencies = n())

greenest_table <- greenest |>
  left_join(size_medians, join_by(size)) |>
  mutate(times_below_median = median_lbs_per_trip / lbs_per_trip) |>
  arrange(match(size, c("Large", "Medium", "Small"))) |>
  select(size, `Agency Name`, lbs_per_trip, median_lbs_per_trip,
         times_below_median)
```

I calculated this award by comparing each agency's total CO2 emissions per passenger trip. I selected the agency with the lowest emissions in each size category (small, medium, and large). I also compared each winner to the median emissions of agencies in its size group to determine how many times lower its emissions were than the typical agency.

```{r}
greenest_table |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(size = "Size Group", `Agency Name` = "Winner",
             lbs_per_trip = "Winner (lbs CO2 per trip)",
             median_lbs_per_trip = "Median Agency (lbs CO2 per trip)",
             times_below_median = "Times Below Median") |>
  fmt_number(c(lbs_per_trip, median_lbs_per_trip), decimals = 2) |>
  fmt_number(times_below_median, decimals = 1) |>
  tab_source_note("Source: National Transit Database; U.S. Energy Information Administration")
```

### Award 2 (our own): The Dirtiest Large System

```{r}
large_median_mile <- agency_summary |>
  filter(size == "Large") |>
  summarize(m = median(lbs_per_mile)) |>
  pull(m)

dirtiest <- agency_summary |>
  filter(size == "Large") |>
  arrange(desc(lbs_per_mile)) |>
  head(3) |>
  mutate(large_median = large_median_mile) |>
  select(`Agency Name`, lbs_per_mile, large_median, lbs_per_trip)
```

I chose this award to identify large transit agencies with the highest CO2 emissions per passenger mile. I filtered the data to include only large agencies and ranked them from highest to lowest emissions per passenger mile. Since it accounts for both emissions and the distance passengers travel, it's useful for identifying systems that produce relatively high emissions compared to their passenger usage.

```{r}
dirtiest |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(`Agency Name` = "Agency",
             lbs_per_mile = "lbs CO2 per Passenger Mile",
             large_median = "Median Large Agency (lbs CO2 per Mile)",
             lbs_per_trip = "lbs CO2 per Trip") |>
  fmt_number(c(lbs_per_mile, large_median, lbs_per_trip), decimals = 2) |>
  tab_source_note("Source: National Transit Database; U.S. Energy Information Administration")
```
